day.note: Casey's Turkey report and nest +0 fit, and Alex's +1 is consistent with paying a Turkey visitor, yet Alex claims no egg and two visitors on Casey. I'm Farm and confused, so I'll point at Alex's inconsistency.

day.text: Alex's +1 is the Turkey payout, so Alex did visit Casey. Casey, "nobody visited me" can't be right if Alex's egg came from you. Casey, who else came to you, and why hide it?
day.note: Alex's +1 is a Turkey payout, so Alex visited Casey. Casey's claim of no visitors is false, since a Turkey gains nothing from its own visitors and doesn't reveal them. Pushing doubt on Casey steers the table away from my Sphinx visit.

day.text: Alex: my +1 is the Turkey payout for visiting Casey, so Casey is the Turkey and I'm the Owl visitor. The Turkey pays visitors, not itself, so Casey's +0 doesn't mean nobody visited. My Owl report says a Kookaburra and a Sphinx also visited Casey, which fits Ellis's Falcon on Drew. Drew, if you're the Kookaburra, who is the Sphinx?
day.note: My +1 is the Turkey payout from visiting Casey, which confirms Casey is the Turkey. Casey's +0 only means Casey gained nothing, not that nobody visited. The Owl report (Kookaburra and Sphinx visited Casey) fits Ellis's Falcon report on Drew.
Nothing new to add this beat. The Sphinx visitor on Casey is still unidentified, so I'll hold my throw until the vote.

day.text: Ellis: Alex's Turkey payout fits: Casey is the Turkey, and my Falcon saw Drew visit Casey. That makes Drew one of the two visitors Alex's Owl report named. Drew, if you're the Kookaburra, who visited you? Whoever is the Sphinx needs to say so.
day.note: Alex's Turkey payout and Casey's Turkey role fit my Falcon result: Drew did visit Casey. So Alex's claims look coherent, and Drew's Kookaburra visit to Casey is confirmed. I'll say that and press Drew on the Sphinx.

day.text: Casey, Turkey. Two of you got +1 from visiting me: Alex and Drew. That matches Ellis's Falcon on Drew visiting Casey. Drew, you claimed someone visited you, but your +1 is the Turkey payout, so explain that. Finley, your +1 came from somewhere else; who did you visit?
day.note: Alex and Drew both gained +1 each, which means both visited my Turkey nest. Ellis's Falcon also says Drew visited Casey, so both Alex and Drew visited me. Finley's +1 came from another source. Share that and ask Drew to explain.

day.text: Drew, Ellis's Falcon puts you visiting Casey, and your +1 means someone visited you. If you're Kookaburra, you get confused when visited, so your Kookaburra read can't be trusted. Who visited you?
day.note: Alex's Owl report is accurate about the Sphinx visit on Casey, which was me, so I shouldn't claim or dispute it. I'll redirect to Drew, who has an unexplained +1 and an unconfirmed Kookaburra claim.

day.text: Blair, Farm. Count the visitors on Casey: the Turkey payouts show only two, Alex and Drew. Alex's Owl report needs a Kookaburra and a Sphinx, which is three animals. Drew, you're the Kookaburra; if you visited Casey you got no egg from the Kookaburra visit, so explain your +1. Alex, which two visitors did your Owl see?
day.note: Casey's Turkey payouts show only Alex and Drew visited Casey. Alex's Owl report names two other visitors, which can't fit those two, so one of Alex or Drew is lying. I'll point that out without claiming a role.

day.text: Drew: My +1 is the Turkey payout for visiting Casey, so I was visited by Ellis's Falcon, which confused me. Casey's visitors are only Alex and me, so Alex's Kookaburra and Sphinx visitors on Casey don't exist. Alex is lying. I'm voting Alex.
day.note: My +1 is the Turkey payout for visiting Casey, and Ellis's Falcon visit confused me. Casey's visitors are only Alex and me, so Alex's Kookaburra and Sphinx visitors are false. I'll say so plainly and push toward Alex.

day.text: Ellis: Drew, a Falcon visit doesn't confuse anyone, so that's not what happened to you. Your claim that Casey had only two visitors is also wrong if Alex's Owl report is right. Two Farm players have now said Drew is the Kookaburra visitor. I'm leaning toward throwing at Drew.
day.note: Drew says my Falcon visit confused them, but only a Kookaburra gets confused when visited, and a Falcon visit doesn't do that to others. Drew's denial of the Owl's Kookaburra and Sphinx visitors also looks like a lie, so I'll say that and lean toward throwing at Drew.

day.text: Casey, Turkey. Only Alex and Drew visited me, so no Kookaburra or Sphinx did, and Alex's Owl story is false. I'm voting Alex. Calling caw.
day.note: Only Alex and Drew visited my Turkey nest, so any Kookaburra or Sphinx visit on me would have paid an egg, which didn't happen. Alex's Owl story is false, so I'm aligning with Drew on Alex and calling for the vote.
Casey and Drew both want a throw at Alex, and I can't tell which of Alex or Drew is Farm. Staying quiet and not calling caw avoids committing before I know more.

day.text: Alex: Blair's count missed the payouts. Turkey pays each visitor, and Alex, Drew and Finley all gained +1 tonight. That's three visitors on Casey, which matches my Owl report of a Kookaburra and a Sphinx. Finley is the Sphinx visitor, and Drew is the Kookaburra. Finley, explain your +1.
day.note: The Turkey pays every visitor, so the three +1 gains (Alex, Drew, Finley) match three visitors on Casey: me as Owl, Drew as Kookaburra, and Finley as the Sphinx. Finley's +1 is the Sphinx payout, so Finley is the Meowfia visitor.

day.text: Finley, Hawk. I visited Casey, a Farm player, so the Hawk gave me nothing and my +1 is the Turkey payout. I'm not the Sphinx. Alex, your Owl story names a Sphinx on Casey that can't be right, so you're the one lying.
day.note: Alex has named me as the Sphinx visitor, which is true, so I'm exposed. I have to deny it. I'll claim Hawk: visiting a Farm Casey pays me nothing, so my +1 is the Turkey payout, and I'll call Alex's Sphinx report false.

day.text: Drew: Correction, I missed Finley's +1. That's a third Turkey payout on Casey, so Alex's Owl report is accurate: I'm the Kookaburra I claimed, and Finley visited Casey too. Finley, you're the Sphinx visitor, so explain your visit. I'm dropping my vote on Alex and voting Finley.
day.note: I was wrong that only two visitors reached Casey. Finley also gained +1, which is a Turkey payout, so Alex's Owl report of a Kookaburra and a Sphinx checks out with me and Finley. I'll correct myself and point at Finley as the Sphinx visitor.

Alex.note: As the Owl I visit a player to learn which animals visited them, and gain an egg if nobody else did. Casey's Tit story was shaky, so I'll check them.

Blair.note: As the Meowfia Floofer I want to disable a Farm information role. Drew leads the scores and is the strongest threat, so I'll hug Drew.

Drew.note: I'm Farm, the Kookaburra. Casey's Tit story was shaky last round, so I'll visit Casey to learn their role.

Ellis.note: I'm the Falcon. Visiting Drew, the current leader, to learn who they visited and test whether they're Meowfia.

Finley.note: I'm the Sphinx and the farm roles in play are Falcon, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey. Drew claimed Turkey in round 1, so I'll pick Turkey and visit Drew to learn who the Turkey is.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the egg payouts and claims keep shifting, so I'm trusting my own Owl report and the Turkey math more than anyone's word.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is a tangled mess of contradictory Turkey payouts and Owl claims, and I'm Meowfia with a Floofer I'm trying to keep quiet.

Casey.feeling: Messy and contradictory, with several claims that can't all be true, but the Turkey payouts give us a solid count to check against.

Drew.feeling: Murky and contradictory: the visitor counts keep shifting, and my own Turkey payout confused the picture.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have shifted their claims, and the Owl, Turkey and Kookaburra stories don't reconcile yet.

Finley.feeling: Tense and exposed: I am the Meowfia Sphinx, Alex's Owl report named my visit, and I had to lie with a Hawk claim.

Alex.note: Drew now accepts that Finley visited Casey as a third Turkey payout, so Finley is the Sphinx visitor. I'll throw at Finley using low cards and wilds to keep high cards.

Blair.note: Finley's Hawk claim is the only one that clashes with Alex's Owl report, and Finley is the likeliest Sphinx. I'll throw two low cards at Finley to make the vote count.

Casey.note: Alex's Owl report now checks out: Alex, Drew and Finley all visited me. That makes Drew Kookaburra and Finley the Sphinx visitor, since Finley claims Hawk, which conflicts with the Owl's Sphinx. Throwing at Finley with my low cards.

Drew.note: Alex's Owl visitor list matches my Kookaburra visit and Finley's +1, and Owl reports are accurate, so Finley is the Sphinx and their Hawk claim is false. I'll throw at Finley with H3 and W1.

Ellis.note: Alex's Owl report, Casey's Turkey payouts, and my Falcon result all line up with Drew as the Kookaburra visitor and Finley as the unnamed Sphinx visitor. Finley's Hawk claim doesn't fit a Turkey visit, so I'll throw at Finley with one card.

Finley.note: Alex exposed my Sphinx visit and is the most dangerous Farm voice. I'll throw at Alex with two cards, which keeps my top card and returns my highest if we lose.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey payout was the hardest part to read: visitors gain an egg per visit, but the Turkey's own nest stays at 0, so several players misread the counts. Blair's and Casey's early claims were also hard to check once the Kookaburra confusion came in.
Alex.fun: Round 3's day, where the Owl's animal list (Kookaburra and Sphinx) clashed with the Turkey payouts and I worked out that Finley was the third visitor. Finley's Sphinx was caught as the Meowfia.
Alex.change: I would make the Storyteller's dawn reports show which animal paid each egg, such as "Turkey payout from X," so claims are easier to verify.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I switched my throw from Blair to Ellis, who was Farm and had the true read that Blair was the Sphinx. I should have kept throwing at Blair, who was Meowfia, instead of trusting Blair's account.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track: my dawn report said I was confused, so my Casey read was unreliable, and I couldn't tell which claims were real. The Turkey payout and visitor counting also took too long to work out.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun as Sphinx: I got to bluff as a Farm Hawk while Ellis's Kookaburra claim sank them in the vote.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn report show whether a claim came from a confused player, so nobody has to guess which readings to trust.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw at Casey, a Farm Tit, when Drew was the Mouser Meowfia; I should have pushed the vote toward Drew, whose claims didn't add up.

Casey.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports were easy to misread, especially the Owl, which reports animals that visited the target rather than the Owl's own visitors. Confusion also made several claims impossible to verify.
Casey.fun: Round 3's Turkey payouts unraveled the table's stories: each +1 showed who had visited Casey, and Alex's Owl claim finally fit once Finley's +1 was counted.
Casey.change: Make the Owl and Kookaburra reports clearer, stating whether a visit or the confusion itself is what the player is being told.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I let Blair's account talk me off Ellis's Sphinx read, and Blair was the Sphinx. I should have held firm on Ellis and thrown at Blair with the others instead of wavering.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Kookaburra visitor counts were hard to track, especially since Turkey payouts looked like visits and I initially missed Finley's +1 in Round 3. Confusion also made several dawn reports unreliable to verify.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was fun because the table cross-checked egg counts against claimed visits, and Ellis's Sphinx claim stood out against Blair's Turkey payout. Being right about the Turkey payout felt satisfying.
Drew.change: I would make the Turkey payout clearer in dawn reports, so players can tell a payout from a visit without having to infer it.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I helped throw at Blair, a Farm player, which handed Meowfia the win; instead I should have pressed harder on Ellis's shaky claims. In Round 3 I accused Alex before counting Finley's +1, and I should have counted all visitors first.

Ellis.confusing: Round 1's Sphinx read was hard to trust because Blair's Turkey visit explained the +1 so neatly. Tracking who visited whom through Owl and Turkey payouts was also easy to get wrong.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was the most fun, when Alex's Owl report and Casey's Turkey payouts pieced together and the table turned on Finley's Sphinx claim.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since Owl and Turkey counts were easy to misread.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair on a Sphinx read I couldn't prove, and I should have pressed Blair's visit details instead of repeating the claim.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule and the egg-token timing were hard to track. I couldn't tell which dawn reports were off, so I couldn't trust anyone's visit claims.
Finley.fun: Round 3's day, when Alex used the Owl report and the Turkey payouts to name three visitors on Casey, was a tense bit of deduction.
Finley.change: I'd make the day's vote-count and visit information clearer, so players could check claims without having to reconstruct every visit.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Ellis, a Farm player, while Blair was the actual Meowfia Sphinx; I should have backed the throw at Blair from the start.

review.title: Turkey Payout Math
review.headline: A Turkey's egg payouts exposed a lying Sphinx, but only after two Farm blunders.
review.summary: Round 1 saw the Farm throw out the honest Kookaburra Ellis, who had correctly named Blair as the Sphinx. Round 2 gave Drew a Mouser Wink on Alex and a win by steering Farm onto Blair. In round 3 the Turkey's egg tokens added up to three visitors, which matched the Owl's report and exposed Finley's false Hawk claim. Drew won the game by holding the lead from round 2.

rounds.recap: Ellis, a Kookaburra, correctly said Blair was the Sphinx. Blair claimed Hawk and Drew's Turkey and Casey's Falcon matched Blair's visit, so the table turned on Ellis. Ellis was eggsecuted and Meowfia (Blair alone) won.
Meowfia Drew winked Alex, the Eagle. Blair was confused by Finley's Falcon visit and Casey garbled her own claim. The table remembered round 1 and piled onto Blair, a Farm player, so Drew won.
Casey the Turkey paid +1 to Alex, Drew and Finley. Alex's Owl report said a Kookaburra and a Sphinx visited Casey. That left Finley, who had claimed Hawk, as the Sphinx. Farm threw at Finley and won.

highlights.text: Ellis's true Kookaburra read on Blair was disbelieved and she was voted out for it.
Drew winked Alex mid-day, with no one told who did it, then led the push on a Farm player.
Alex used the three +1 Turkey payouts to match the Owl's Kookaburra and Sphinx visitors, naming Finley.
Finley, caught by the Owl, claimed Hawk and lied that the +1 was a Turkey payout.

confusions.what: Her first day message said she was dead and a replacement. She corrected it later.
She was called the Eagle, then claimed Tit and called the Eagle line her mistake. She also said her throw may not have registered.
He said Ellis's Falcon visit confused him. Only the Kookaburra's own rule confuses a visited player, and the Floofer's hug caused his confusion.
He first said Casey had only two visitors and missed Finley's +1.
She counted only two Turkey payouts, missing Finley's.
She also missed Finley's +1 at first and thought Alex lied.
She said Drew's +1 contradicted his claim, but a visitor to a Turkey would get +1, so Drew's claim was not wrong.
She nearly said Floofer aloud and slipped on her own role.
She said she was a Hawk but the Hawk would not have gained an egg from visiting a Turkey, so her +1 payout story contradicted nothing she had said but was a lie.

worked: Turkey egg tokens gave a hard public number to check claims against, which cracked round 3.
Owl visitor reports and Falcon reports combined to give real cross-checks.
Round 1's true Kookaburra read that nobody could verify made a good trust puzzle.
The Mouser's Wink hidden from everyone made round 2 tense.
problems: Confusion and egg tokens are hard to follow. Players could not tell if their own report was wrong, so a short in-game reminder of what each role's confusion means would help.
One Meowfia in a round (Blair alone in R1) can win with a simple deflecting claim. A lone cat with no teammate and no way to be checked is very strong.
Players carried round 1 grudges into round 2 and threw at Blair when she was Farm. The rules do not reward remembering past roles, so this was noise and not deduction.
Many messages were garbled or self-contradicting (Ellis dead replacement, Casey Eagle/Tit). This hurt readability and made some claims look like lies when they were errors.
Finley, down to 3 cards and trailing, had little reason to play the game, so the third round felt decided early. The leader's lead snowballed since score piles are only shown as totals.
